claims.title: Termination void — protected period
claims.finding: Termination was served on day 12 of a medically certified incapacity. In the 2nd–5th year of service the protected period is 90 days. Notice served during a protected period is VOID (nichtig) — the employment relationship legally continues.
claims.valueBasis: Wage continuation claim, 2 months' gross salary (conservative)

citations.holding: Notice given during the Art. 336c protected period is void and produces no legal effect.
Protected period during illness: 30 days (1st year), 90 days (years 2–5), 180 days (from year 6).
Employer bears consequences of void notice; wage claim persists during continued employment.

claims.title: Unpaid overtime
claims.finding: 89 documented overtime hours, never compensated in time or money. Statutory rate: hourly wage + 25% supplement unless validly waived in writing. Contract contains no valid waiver clause.
claims.valueBasis: 89h × CHF 45.00 × 1.25 ≈ CHF 5,006; claimed conservatively at CHF 4,000 net of disputed hours

citations.holding: Overtime compensation: 25% supplement applies absent valid written agreement to the contrary.

claims.title: Reference letter (Arbeitszeugnis) not issued
claims.finding: Employee has an unconditional statutory right to a full, benevolent and truthful reference letter at any time. None was issued. Courts assign this claim a dispute value of approximately one month's salary.
claims.valueBasis: Dispute value convention: ~½–1 monthly salary (Zurich court practice)

citations.holding: Rule of thumb: reference letter claim = 1 monthly salary dispute value.

prewrittenMemo:
LEGAL ASSESSMENT MEMORANDUM

Re: Meier v. TechCorp AG — Termination during protected period

I. SUMMARY
The termination served on 26 June 2026 is void under Art. 336c para. 1(b) OR. Ms Meier was on day 12 of a medically certified incapacity; in her fourth year of service the law grants a 90-day protected period. Notice served within it produces no legal effect (BGE 134 III 354). The employment relationship therefore legally continues, grounding a wage-continuation claim conservatively valued at two months' gross salary (CHF 15,600).

II. SECONDARY CLAIMS
(1) Overtime, Art. 321c OR: 89 documented hours, no valid written waiver; claim CHF 4,000 (conservative). (2) Reference letter, Art. 330a OR: unconditional entitlement; none issued; dispute value per Zurich practice ~CHF 3,800.

III. TOTAL & PROCEDURE
Total claim: CHF 23,400 — within the simplified, cost-free procedure (< CHF 30,000, Art. 113/114 ZPO). Mandatory conciliation applies; hearings are typically scheduled within two months. Cantonal data indicate ~60% of employment claims resolve at conciliation; prepared claimants settle at materially higher rates.

IV. RECOMMENDED STRATEGY
Dispatch written objection (Art. 336b OR) and demand letter within 48 hours. Absent settlement, file conciliation request by 15 September 2026. Client to be prepared via hearing rehearsal (personal appearance mandatory, Art. 204 ZPO).

All findings cited to sources retrieved via Omnilex. Subject to review and signature by supervising counsel.
